findings.title: Liquidated damages calculated on total contract value
findings.deviation: The clause calculates liquidated damages at 1% of the total Contract Value per week instead of the affected milestone fee, sets the cap at 10% of the total Contract Value, does not exclude client-caused delays, and is not stated as the sole and exclusive remedy.
findings.impact: AtliQ could face disproportionate penalties based on the entire project value for delays, including those caused by the client, without a sole remedy limitation.
findings.quote: Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay. The aggregate liquidated damages payable under this Clause 12 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Contract Value.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client; LDs are the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Uncapped data protection liability
findings.deviation: The aggregate liability cap explicitly carves out and excludes breaches of Clause 13 (Data Protection), leading to unlimited liability for data protection and security incidents.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces unlimited financial exposure for any alleged breaches of data protection laws or security incidents under the contract.
findings.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual aggregate liability capped at 1× fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months, with data protection liability subject to a separate super-cap of 2× fees.

findings.title: Payment limited to accepted work on convenience termination
findings.deviation: Upon termination for convenience by the Company, AtliQ is only entitled to payment for services performed and accepted, which excludes unaccepted work-in-progress.
findings.impact: AtliQ may not receive compensation for work-in-progress or unbilled services if the client terminates the agreement early for convenience.
findings.quote: The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice, in which event the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period.

fine.note: IP ownership and licensing terms match the approved standard: client owns deliverables upon payment, and AtliQ retains background IP with a non-exclusive license.
Confidentiality terms are mutual with standard survival obligations.
Indemnification is balanced and subject to the contract's aggregate liability cap, which is highly favorable.
The contract does not impose any non-compete or non-solicitation restrictions on AtliQ.
No onerous insurance limits or certification requirements are imposed.
Deductions are restricted only to liquidated damages under this agreement, which is acceptable.
Milestone acceptance requirements are standard and acceptable.
Data protection obligations under Clause 13 are standard; the liability exception is addressed under the liability topic.
